thread.title: Cat Leads Dow As Apple Pares Gains; Chance To Buy Buffett Stocks

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Cat Leads Dow As Apple Pares Gains; Chance To Buy Buffett Stocks
text:
A key   ETF led Thursday as Caterpillar ( CAT ) and United Technologies ( UTX ) rallied. But Apple ( AAPL ) and other big-cap techs pared some of their gains.
X SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ( DIA ) rose 0.8%, SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ) added 0.2% and PowerShares QQQ Trust ( QQQ ) inched up less than 0.1% in the stock market today . Caterpillar and United Technologies led the Dow with respective gains of 2.2% and 3.2%.
Energy, real estate and utilities were among the top sector fund gainers, while banks, telecom and biotechs lagged. Tech stocks backed off from earlier gains. Technology Select Sector SPDR ( XLK ) was up 0.1%. It remains in potential buy range from a rebound off its 50-day line. However, it suffered a sharp drop to the   early February market rout.
XLK's top holdings include Apple, which rose 0.8% as it attempts to rise further above the 50-day, where it's been trading near for a fifth straight session. The iPhone maker's shares are 4% below a record high. Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Facebook ( FB ) held small gains.
Bitcoin fell 4% to $10,043.32, according to CoinDesk . The cryptocurrency got close to $11,000 earlier. Bitcoin Investment Trust ( GBTC ) gapped down and fell 7% as it continues to meet resistance at its 50-day line, which it breached one month ago.
Buffett Banks If you're looking for a chance to buy top financial stocks owned by Warren Buffett, such as Bank   Goldman Sachs ( GS ), you just might be in luck.
Financial Select Sector SPDR ( XLF ) sliced through   on Feb. 5 as the broader market sold off. But it soon found support, rebounded above the line and remains in a possible buy zone from the 50-day. Shares rose 16% from a late November bounce off the line to their  
The $33.1 billion fund, which celebrated its 19th year in December, tracks the Financial Select Sector Index. Top holdings as of Feb. 20 included JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ), as well as Buffett holdings (as of Q4) Bank of America, Wells Fargo ( WFC ), U.S. Bancorp ( USB ) and Goldman Sachs. Another top name in XLF is the billionaire investor's Berkshire Hathaway ( BRKB ).
The ETF's year-to-date performance of 3.5% is ahead of the S&P 500's 1% gain. XLF's average annual returns of 15.5% and 17.1%, respectively, have outpaced the broader index's 11.1% and 14.8% gains over the past there and five years. But respective returns of 4.8% and 5.8% over the past 10 and 15 years trail the S&P 500's 9.5% and 10.4% gains for those same periods.
Bank stocks got a big boost following President Trump's election in November 2016, and have trended mostly higher since. They are expected to be beneficiaries of higher interest rates, which have also boosted many of the stocks. XLF carries a 0.13% expense ratio.
